title: Sable and the Inheritance
premise: Cyrus Coldharbour, the reclusive coroner of the river town of Marrow's Bend, is pulled into an investigation when a drowned stranger washes up wearing clothes stolen from his own closet — a message meant for him alone. The dead man turns out to be connected to the estate of Cyrus's late mentor, Judge Ellery Sable, whose contested will has the town at each other's throats. As Cyrus decodes a ledger hidden in the judge's gravestone rubbings, he uncovers that the judge falsified a death verdict decades ago to protect someone Cyrus loves, and that the killer is silencing everyone who could reopen the case. In the end, Cyrus must choose between loyalty to the person who raised him and the truth he swore to speak over every grave; he testifies, the true heir is named, and Cyrus finally lets himself be seen.
about_author: Ines Dunmore is the pen name of a former small-town court clerk who spent eleven years transcribing testimony in a courthouse older than the county itself. She writes mysteries about quiet people forced into the light, and lives within walking distance of three cemeteries she can name by heart.

chapters.title: The Man in My Clothes
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. A drowned stranger is pulled from the Bend wearing Cyrus's own missing coat, shirt, and boots. The uncanny intimacy of dressing a body in your own garments unsettles him deeply. Emotional beat: dread disguised as professional calm.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. Cyrus walks the cemetery cataloguing the dead as he does nightly, establishing his ritual invisibility and his encyclopedic memory of the town's deaths. He notices fresh flowers on Judge Sable's grave — placed by no one he knows. Emotional beat: loneliness revealed through tenderness.

chapters.title: The Will That Wouldn't Settle
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. The reading of Ellery Sable's contested will: the judge left everything to 'the one who kept my ledger,' naming no one. Rival heirs — the judge's nephew Aldous and housekeeper Ruth Vane — circle each other. Emotional beat: suspicion taking root.

chapters.title: A Ledger Hidden in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. Among Sable's effects Cyrus finds a coroner's logbook with impossible entries — dates of deaths that never happened, initials where names should be. He realizes the judge left him a puzzle deliberately. Emotional beat: reluctant curiosity becoming compulsion.

chapters.title: The Witness Nobody Saw
chapters.summary: POV Deputy Mara Quist. Mara interviews townsfolk about the drowned man and realizes Cyrus was seen near the river the night before the body surfaced. She likes him but files what she saw. Emotional beat: duty straining against affection.

chapters.title: Gravestone Rubbings
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. Following a hunch, Cyrus takes charcoal rubbings of Sable's headstone and matches the carved dates to the phantom ledger entries. The stones record two deaths apiece — one real, one invented. Emotional beat: awe curdling into fear.

chapters.title: Aldous Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. Nephew Aldous Sable, charming and desperate, offers Cyrus money to declare the ledger a forgery before probate trial. Cyrus refuses, and Aldous's charm slips just enough to show teeth. Emotional beat: temptation met and refused.

chapters.title: What Ruth Carried
chapters.summary: POV Ruth Vane. The housekeeper remembers the night thirty years ago when the judge came home soaked to the bone, burning papers, whispering about the millpond. She has kept one scorched page ever since. Emotional beat: guilt as inheritance.

chapters.title: The Millpond Verdict
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. The ledger's pattern points to 1994: a drowning the judge ruled accidental that was nothing of the kind. The victim's name has been chiseled off the family monument. Emotional beat: the past pressing its hand flat against the present.

chapters.title: Someone in the Archive
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Mara finds the county archive ransacked — the 1994 file gone — and catches a figure fleeing who moves like someone who knows the building blindfolded. She begins to suspect the killer is local, old, and trusted. Emotional beat: the safe turning strange.

chapters.title: Threats Written in Chalk
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. A chalk outline of a body appears on Cyrus's morgue floor, drawn around empty space, with the ledger's cipher repeated beside it. Whoever it is knows exactly how far he's gotten. Emotional beat: invisibility revoked.

chapters.title: Ruth's Scorched Page
chapters.summary: POV Ruth. Ruth gives Cyrus the burned fragment: half a confession in the judge's hand, naming 'my boy' as witness. Cyrus realizes the judge protected him all these years — and that the truth endangers him most of all. Emotional beat: love and betrayal entangled.

chapters.title: The Second Body
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. The town archivist who handled the 1994 records is found dead of apparent heart failure — a death only Cyrus recognizes as staged, because he taught the archivist's daughter how hearts actually stop. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into resolve.

chapters.title: Mara Asks the Wrong Question
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Mara confronts Cyrus about the night by the river; he admits he received an anonymous letter luring him there, which he'd hidden out of shame. Trust between them fractures and reforms on new terms. Emotional beat: honesty as costly relief.

chapters.title: Deciphering the Cipher
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. Working nights, Cyrus cracks the ledger's substitution scheme — it maps onto hymn numbers from Sable's old funeral book. The decoded column lists not deaths but payments, made annually to silence a survivor. Emotional beat: triumph shadowed by foreboding.

chapters.title: The Survivor
chapters.summary: POV Ruth. Ruth identifies the payee: a child who survived the millpond, smuggled away and paid for lifelong — the judge's illegitimate grandchild, the true heir. Ruth confesses she helped hide the child. Emotional beat: confession as unburdening.

chapters.title: Trial Week Begins
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. Probate trial opens; Aldous's lawyer moves to have the ledger excluded as forgery. Cyrus is subpoenaed as expert witness, meaning his findings — and his secrets — will be dragged into open court. Emotional beat: cornered clarity.

chapters.title: The Letter's Return Address
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Mara traces the anonymous letter's paper stock to the funeral home owned by the judge's oldest friend, mortician Wendell Pryce — the man who prepared both the 1994 body and the drowned stranger. Emotional beat: the horror of familiar faces.

chapters.title: Pryce's Quiet Room
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. Cyrus confronts Wendell Pryce, who reveals the drowned man was a blackmailer hired by Aldous, killed when he demanded more — and that Pryce dressed him in Cyrus's clothes to warn Cyrus off. Emotional beat: pity for a broken accomplice.

chapters.title: Testimony Over the Grave
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. On the stand, Cyrus presents the decoded ledger, the rubbings, and the 1994 fraud, then names the surviving heir — knowing it exposes the judge's crimes and his own years of silence. Emotional beat: truth chosen over loyalty at last.

chapters.title: What the Stones Say Now
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Aldous is arrested for the blackmail-murder; Pryce cooperates; the court names the heir, who arrives quietly and asks only to see the graves. Mara and Cyrus stand watch together, colleagues now in truth. Emotional beat: justice without triumphalism.

chapters.title: Sable and the Inheritance
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. Cyrus carves a replacement stone restoring the erased name, adds the heir's lineage beneath Sable's, and for the first time signs the cemetery register instead of slipping away unseen. Emotional beat: peace earned by being witnessed.
